memos.headline: MSFT and XOM Lead on Relative Strength; CAT and UNH Breaking Down
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe today. MSFT is the standout leader with +23% relative strength vs SPY over 4 weeks, trading 15.1% above its 50-day mean after a +26.6% monthly surge—this is a powerful momentum thrust, though the extension raises near-term pullback risk. XOM is the cleanest trend, sitting just 3.7% off its 52w high with RSI 67.9 and positive relative strength across both 4w (+1.6%) and 12w (+9.6%) windows, well above both moving averages. On the other side, CAT is the weakest name in the group at -22.3% drawdown from highs, -8.6% below its 50d mean, and -11.0% relative strength vs SPY over 12 weeks—a clear downtrend. UNH is similarly deteriorating with RSI 38.3, -5.7% below its 50d mean, and -10.9% 4w relative strength, suggesting the 26w uptrend is rolling over.

views.note: Massive 4w relative strength of +23% vs SPY and 12w +15.1% confirms institutional momentum; I'd respect the trend above the 50d mean (~420 area) but the 15% extension warrants tight stops near 460.
Cleanest uptrend in the universe: only -3.7% from 52w high, +10.8% above 50d, +15.8% above 200d, with positive relative strength on all timeframes; would reassess on a close below 155.
Strong 12w relative strength (+15.4%) and tight -3.7% drawdown from highs, but 4w relative strength has turned negative (-4.1%) and RSI 48.5 is middling; needs to hold 340 to stay constructive.
Flat relative strength vs SPY over 4w and 12w with RSI 51 right at midline; no edge either way until it breaks above the 52w high zone (~236) or loses the 200d mean area (~195).
Sitting right on its 50d mean with RSI 47 but 4w relative strength of -10.7% vs SPY is concerning; would turn constructive above 320 or cautious below 295.
Worst drawdown in the group at -22.3% from highs, -8.6% below 50d mean, RSI 42.8, and -11.0% 12w relative strength vs SPY—a clear downtrend with no sign of stabilization.
RSI 38.3 is the lowest in the universe, -5.7% below 50d mean, and 4w relative strength of -10.9% signals the prior uptrend is breaking; would reconsider only above 415.
Trading below both 50d and 200d means, -13.5% from 52w high, negative 26w return of -9.6%—a persistent laggard with no technical catalyst to own.
12w relative strength of -13.4% is ugly but 4w has turned positive at +4.2%, suggesting possible base-building near 340; needs to reclaim 360 for conviction.
Mixed signals with strong 26w return (+30.1%) but negative 12w return (-4.9%) and middling RSI 49.7; watching for a break above 270 to confirm the 4w bounce has legs.

memos.headline: Mega-cap tech earnings power surging; XOM and PG show cash-flow compression that warrants caution
memos.body: I am struck by the breadth of earnings acceleration across the large-cap tech complex this quarter. NVDA posted 85% YoY revenue growth and a 71.5% net margin on $81.6B of revenue, while GOOGL delivered a remarkable 93.7% net margin on $119.8B of revenue with net income up nearly 4x YoY—numbers I want to see sustained before raising conviction further. AMZN's margin expansion to 31.2% (net income +245% YoY) and MSFT's 39.7% net margin on 17.7% revenue growth confirm durable earnings power in cloud/AI-driven businesses. On the other side, XOM's net income fell 46% YoY to $4.2B on essentially flat revenue with a 4.9% net margin, and PG printed a 16% decline in net income on just 1.5% top-line growth—classic cash-flow compression profiles I want to avoid. CAT surprised positively with 24% revenue growth and 65% net income growth, though I need to see whether the backlog supports durability before getting more constructive.

views.note: 85% YoY revenue growth, 71.5% net margin, and minimal debt ($8.5B) represent extraordinary earnings power; would reassess if margins compress below 55%.
Full-year 10-K shows 39.7% net margin and 17.7% revenue growth with moderate $40B debt, confirming durable cloud/AI-driven profitability.
Net margin expanded to 31.2% on $200.6B revenue with net income up 245% YoY, though $133B total debt warrants monitoring.
93.7% net margin and 298% net income growth are extraordinary but likely include one-time items; I need segment detail to raise conviction.
16.4% revenue growth and 27.2% net margin show re-acceleration, but $82.3B debt load and hardware cyclicality temper enthusiasm.
27.7% revenue growth and 36.9% net margin are strong for a bank, but cycle-dependent earnings and $461B debt keep me neutral until credit quality data is clearer.
24% revenue growth and 17.5% net margin are impressive, but cyclical industrials need backlog visibility before I get constructive.
Revenue essentially flat (+0.4% YoY) with a thin 4.9% net margin despite 61% net income recovery; need to see sustained top-line growth.
Net income down 46% YoY to $4.2B on a 4.9% net margin signals commodity-driven cash-flow compression; would revisit only if margins recover above 8%.
Net income fell 15.8% on just 1.5% revenue growth with a 14.4% net margin—pricing power appears exhausted and earnings are compressing.

memos.headline: Fed on Pause at 3.75% but Sticky 3.3% CPI and Rising Long Yields Favor Value over Duration
memos.body: I see a clear pause regime: the Fed has held the upper bound at 3.75% for three months after cutting 75 bp over the prior year, while headline CPI is running at 3.3% YoY—still well above target and likely keeping the FOMC sidelined. The labor market is firm with unemployment at 4.10%, down 20 bp over both three- and twelve-month horizons, which removes any urgency to ease further. The 10-year yield at 4.74%, up 41 bp YoY and 17 bp over three months, signals the long end is repricing for persistent inflation and fiscal supply; the 10y-2y spread at +50 bp confirms a normally sloped but flattening curve. This backdrop is unfriendly to long-duration growth equities whose valuations are discounted at higher real rates, while banks benefit from a positive curve and solid loan demand, and energy/cyclicals benefit from nominal growth. A CPI print falling below 3.0% or unemployment rising above 4.4% would shift my call toward an easing-resumption regime favoring growth.

views.note: Positive yield curve, strong labor market, and paused Fed support net interest margins and credit quality.
Nominal growth resilience and sticky inflation historically support energy earnings; firm labor market underpins demand.
Cyclical beneficiary of solid employment and above-trend nominal GDP implied by 3.3% CPI and low unemployment.
Staples offer defensive positioning but limited upside; rising long yields compress the bond-proxy premium.
High-duration growth name faces headwinds from 10y yields at 4.74% and rising; valuation multiples compress in a pause-with-sticky-inflation regime.
Quality compounder but long-duration characteristics limit upside while 10y yields grind higher; not a clear avoid given cash generation.
Similar duration profile to AAPL; recurring revenue provides resilience but rising discount rates cap multiple expansion.
Consumer discretionary exposure plus long-duration AWS growth story both pressured by sticky inflation and elevated long rates.
Ad revenue tied to nominal GDP is a partial offset to duration headwinds; balanced risk-reward in current regime.
Defensive healthcare name with limited macro sensitivity; neither clearly helped nor hurt by current rate-inflation mix.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Split: MSFT and AMZN Surged While AAPL and GOOGL Sold Off Hard — Divergence Creates Opportunities
memos.body: I am reading the post-earnings price reactions as the clearest sentiment signal this cycle. MSFT (+15.5%) and AMZN (+15.3%) saw massive positive reactions to their Q-results filings on 7/29 and 7/30 respectively, suggesting narrative momentum that may still have legs three weeks later. Conversely, AAPL (-7.4%) and GOOGL (-7.1%) were punished sharply on their earnings prints, and with GOOGL filing an additional 8-K on 8/10 (Other Events), the negative tone may not yet be fully washed out. CAT's +5.6% earnings-day pop on 8/4 is a quieter positive signal in an industrial name that typically doesn't attract crowded sentiment, giving me more confidence there. NVDA's 8/17 filing on a material definitive agreement and new financial obligation is fresh and ambiguous — I lack tone data to call direction, so I stay neutral until the market digests it further.

views.note: A +15.5% earnings-day move signals a powerful positive narrative shift that likely still has momentum given the magnitude.
The +15.3% post-earnings reaction on 7/30 is one of the strongest single-day moves in the universe, indicating a decisive sentiment inflection.
A -7.4% earnings-day drop on 7/30 reflects a clear negative sentiment shift that may still be weighing on the stock three weeks later.
The -7.1% earnings sell-off on 7/22 plus a follow-up Other Events 8-K on 8/10 suggest unresolved negative tone around the name.
A clean +5.6% earnings-day pop in a less-crowded industrial name suggests genuine positive sentiment with room to run.
The 8/17 material agreement and new financial obligation filing is too fresh and ambiguous to call direction without clearer tone data.
A modest +2.5% earnings reaction on 7/14 and routine follow-up filings suggest stable but unremarkable sentiment — no strong signal either way.
A mild -1.9% earnings-day dip on 7/29 amid multiple concurrent filings (leadership changes, Reg FD) is noise, not a narrative shift.
A +1.2% earnings reaction on 7/16 is tepid and suggests the market had already priced in the result — no strong directional signal.
The 7/1 filing covers a complex acquisition/disposition event but without an earnings price reaction, I cannot gauge sentiment direction with conviction.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Plunging but Oil Spike and NVDA Reg-FD Filing Flag Residual Geopolitical Risk
memos.body: I note that the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index has collapsed 47.5% over three months to 222.5, and VIX has fallen to 16.01, suggesting the market is pricing out the worst-case policy scenarios around trade and sanctions. However, WTI crude at $89.75 is up 6.4% month-over-month even as it remains down 11.7% over three months, which tells me there is a near-term supply-side tightening—possibly sanctions-related enforcement or OPEC discipline—that has not fully unwound. NVDA's Reg-FD 8-K filed just four days ago (2026-08-17) warrants close attention: in the current export-control environment any forward-looking disclosure could signal new licensing constraints or customer-geography shifts. CAT's early-August Reg-FD filing similarly may reflect updated guidance tied to infrastructure demand or tariff exposure. I have moderate conviction that the structural de-escalation in policy uncertainty is real, but the oil move and semiconductor disclosure cadence keep me cautious on names with concentrated China/energy exposure.

views.note: Recent Reg-FD 8-K amid ongoing AI-chip export-control regime creates binary risk; I need to see the substance before getting constructive.
WTI at $89.75 with a 6.4% monthly rise supports near-term earnings, and falling policy uncertainty reduces windfall-tax tail risk.
Reg-FD disclosure in early August could reflect tariff or infrastructure-bill guidance; the steep prior policy-uncertainty decline helps but 222.5 is still elevated historically.
No new 8-K filings and no direct policy catalyst, but China supply-chain concentration remains a structural overhang that falling uncertainty alone does not resolve.
Steepening yield curve (+11bp 1m) and collapsing policy uncertainty favor large-bank NII; two recent 8-Ks suggest active capital-markets activity.
Defensive compounder benefits from lower policy uncertainty reducing input-cost volatility; three Reg-FD filings in July suggest proactive investor communication.
